text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=runtime-inference-p99-latency, env=prod, region=us-west-2. p99 latency = 2.8s (threshold 2.0s). Pager: @Nina O'Connor. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

PagerDuty: INC12345 triggered by alert rule runtime.p99 > 2s. Auto-escalation in 8m if unacknowledged.

Nina O'Connor: acked on PD, joining. Looking at dashboards now.

Nina O'Connor: top-line — p95 up ~600ms, p99 spike to ~2.8s. Traffic hasn't changed. Request rate steady.

Raj Patel: I'm on latency graphs. I see a sudden increase starting at 12:03 UTC, coincident with a small rollout of runtime v1.14 that bumped batching window from 12ms -> 25ms. Could be batching misconfiguration + sidecar queueing.

Carla Gomez: confirmed rollout window, we pushed a canary to 10% at 12:00 and grad roll started. Canary logs show increased queue depth on the runtime sidecars.

Nina O'Connor: impact? Any customer-facing errors?

Alex H.: No 5xx spike in API, just slower responses. Some clients with tight client-side timeouts reported degraded UX (support tickets trickling in).

Marta (platform-oncall): I'm going to hit the canary rollback toggle to stop the rollout and revert canary to baseline. If that drops p99, rollout caused it.

SRE Runbook Bot: Runbook: latency-spike-general. Steps: 1) Check recent deploys 2) Check queue depth on sidecars 3) Consider temporary rollback or scale sidecars 4) Evaluate KV/cache pressure.

Raj Patel: Running quick queries on sidecar queue depth:
```
# prometheus: avg(queue_depth) across runtime-sidecar pods (last 5m)
runtime_sidecar_queue_depth{pod=~"runtime-sidecar-.*"}  avg_over_time(runtime_sidecar_queue_depth[5m])
=> sample: 180 -> 450 (normal ~40-80)
```

Raj Patel: That confirms queueing. Also seeing increase in sidecar->tokenizer RPC latencies: median 15ms -> 120ms, with some tails at 600ms.

Carla Gomez: Tokenizer service traces show GC spikes around the same time on a subset of tokenizer pods. Looks like tokenizer pods in us-west-2b got a memory pressure GC due to a change in the tokenizer caching layer (LRU eviction threshold tweak) pushed earlier this morning.

Nina O'Connor: So two simultaneous changes: runtime batching window and tokenizer cache tweak. Either alone might be fine, together they amplify.

Nina O'Connor: Priority: reduce customer impact fast. Options: 1) Roll back runtime canary (Marta doing), 2) Scale tokenizer pods + restart the noisy ones, 3) Increase sidecar concurrency/slots temporarily.

Marta (platform-oncall): rollback initiated for runtime v1.14 canary -> v1.13 baseline. Toggling canary off now. ETA 90s for rollout stop.

SRE Runbook Bot: Note: rolling back may stop the added batching window changes. If p99 drops, follow up with safe repro test on staging.

Alex H.: While rollback is in flight, I'll scale tokenizer in us-west-2 from 6 -> 12 replicas to absorb GC pressure and avoid queuing. Doing kubectl scale now.

Alex H.: Command: ```kubectl -n infra scale deploy/tokenizer-uswest2 --replicas=12```

Raj Patel: Restarting the three tokenizer pods with highest RSS (us-west-2b) to clear state. Doing rolling restart: ```kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/tokenizer-uswest2 --field-selector=metadata.name=tokenizer-uswest2-5``` (targeted restarts).

Nina O'Connor: Observability check — watching p99 panels.

(60s pass)

Carla Gomez: rollback completed at 12:06:45 UTC. Canary removed.

Raj Patel: tokenizer scale completed and targeted restarts started.

(2m pass)

Alex H.: Quick metrics: p99 fell to 1.6s and p95 down to 320ms. Queue depth back to ~60 avg.

Nina O'Connor: Excellent. I'll DM customer success to flag impacted customers and add note to status page that degraded performance occurred but resolved; no data loss.

Marta (platform-oncall): Filing a follow-up ticket to block the two risky changes from being co-released without staged rollout checks. Ticket: INF-4621.

Carla Gomez: Root cause hypothesis: tokenizer LRU tweak increased GC tail latency under real traffic, and increased batching window on runtime amplified queuing into tokenizer. Combined effect pushed p99 over SLO.

Raj Patel: Action items: 1) Postmortem-runbook assigned to Raj + Carla + Nina (due 48h), 2) Add runtime batching change to CI perf tests, 3) Add canary gating to require tokenizer health stable before runtime kernel changes.

Nina O'Connor: I'll keep the thread open for 1h to monitor. If stable, I'll close. Great job everyone. :clap:

PagerDuty: INC12345 has been acknowledged by Nina O'Connor.

Incident Bot: Auto-note appended to incident: mitigation = rollback canary + tokenizer scale + targeted restart.

Alex H.: adding debug snippets we used:
```
# check request traces
traceq "service:runtime AND span:tokenizer*" | grep "duration_ms>" | sort -nr | head
# sample slow trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d showing tokenizer wait 540ms
```

Nina O'Connor: Closing checks: p99 stable at 1.4-1.7s for 10m, no new alerts. I'll update the status page and follow up with postmortem. Closing in 20m unless things reappear.

Raj Patel: ACK — noted. Adding timeline notes to the ticket.

SRE Runbook Bot: Reminder: schedule perf regression test for v1.14 against production-like load.

Nina O'Connor: thread closed at 12:28 UTC.
